title: Report incomplete? Find where the scope was lost
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Whole area missing; every subagent succeeded on its brief
Broaden the split; check coverage against the original request
A subagent was asked about the area and came back empty
Improve the search queries or sources
Sources on the area were fetched, then vanished
Fix the analysis brief or filter
Claims reached synthesis but were left out
Adjust what synthesis keeps; report weak support instead of dropping
Gaps only visible after reading the sources
Evaluate the draft for gaps, re-delegate, re-synthesise
rule: If every subagent succeeded and the answer is still missing a whole area, the decomposition was too narrow. Check coverage against the request, not the plan.

title: Subagents wasting effort: overlap, overreach or over-running?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Two subagents fetch the same sources; both feed the report
Partition scope: named source classes and exclusions
Coordinator selects subagents by query complexity
Broad topic, but whole areas missing
Later subagent genuinely needs earlier results
Spawn in sequence; pass complete prior findings
Claims cited to the wrong copy of a source
rule: Overlap between needed subagents is fixed by partitioning scope in the delegation; dropping subagents is for questions that do not need them.

title: Report misses part of the question: where did the gap start?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Part of the request never assigned to a subtask

Evaluate synthesis for gaps, re-delegate, re-synthesise

Two subagents cover the same ground
Simple question runs the full pipeline
rule: Missing from the plan: widen the decomposition. Thin after research: evaluate the synthesis and re-delegate.

title: Pipeline too expensive: which waste is biggest?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Message Batches API (50% off, up to 24h)
rule: Fix the biggest waste first: if most questions are simple, let the coordinator pick only the subagents each one needs.

title: A subagent keeps needing another's help: route it or shortcut it?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Mostly simple, frequent needs (re-read a page, check a fact)
Scoped cross-role tool; complex cases via coordinator
Keep coordinator mediation; structure the request
Subagents talking to each other directly
Subagent given another role's full toolset
Structured error saying what was tried
rule: If a subagent's request can change the plan, it goes through the coordinator; scoped shortcuts are for simple, frequent needs.

title: Report has a hole? Ask when the hole could first have been seen
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Whole areas missing that the request itself implied
Broaden the decomposition (more strands up front)
Missing items surface only inside sources already read
No step checks the draft for gaps
Refinement loop: evaluate synthesis for gaps, re-delegate, re-synthesize
Two helpers research the same ground
Subagent ignores what earlier subagents found
Put complete prior findings in its prompt
Writer needs many small fact checks mid-draft
Scoped cross-role tool for the simple checks
rule: If a gap could only be seen after reading, fix it with a check-the-draft loop, not a bigger plan.

title: Helper needs something from another helper: who decides?
head: Situation
Right mechanism
Why
rows: Follow-up varies and depends on other helpers' results
Return it to the coordinator as structured output
Need is frequent, simple and uniform (e.g. 85% quick lookups)
Scoped cross-role tool for that one need
Saves round trips without losing control
Helpers want to share notes freely
Not a shared store; route via the coordinator
Shared memory bypasses routing and error handling
Independent tasks run one after another
Multiple Task calls in one response
Structured error back to the coordinator
rule: When the next step depends on everyone's work, route it through the coordinator. Give a helper its own cross-role tool only for frequent, simple, uniform needs.

rule: Size the pipeline to the question. The coordinator should invoke only the subagents a request needs.
